messages:
ashley: Heads-up — ran a 24h prod trace on the KV cache behavior for cross-session reuse. Observed steady memory growth (~+3.2GB) on a subset of hosts even though overall request rate was flat. TTL evictions not firing as expected.

pranav: ouch. any idea which keys are sticking around?

ashley: looks like prefix-derived keys from repeated short prompts. We reuse prefix caching across sessions but the key includes session-scoped metadata, so small variations create near-unique keys. fragmentation + no coalescing.

sam: can you paste the key format?

ashley: sure — simplified:
```
cache_key = sha1(model_id || prefix_hash || session_token || seq_start)
```
So session_token is the culprit; it's different per connection but we intended to allow prefix reuse across sessions.

lisa: hmm. that explains the hotset explosion. sequence-level variance also creates many keys. What's traffic distribution?

ashley: 70% short prompts, same prefix patterns across users. Hot prefixes should be shared but are fragmented by session_token. Host-level mem growth correlates with high short-prompt share.

devon: did you profile lookups vs inserts?

ashley: yes. inserts up ~2.1x on affected hosts, lookup hit-rate down ~18% compared to baseline. CPU for eviction scanning rose ~12% due to more entries.

pranav: proposed fix? strip session_token from canonical key and move it to a secondary mapping? or use two-tier keying: prefix fingerprint -> session-bucket?

sam: two-tier sounds reasonable. e.g. primary key = sha1(model_id || prefix_hash) and value contains per-session meta + last-used pointer. That lets reuse across sessions without losing session-specific data.

lisa: downside: still need to bound per-session metadata. we should cap per-prefix per-host session entries and use LRU per session-bucket. Also TTLs need tightening for ephemeral sessions.

ashley: prototype I ran: primary_key = sha1(model + prefix_hash)
secondary_entry id = session_token_short (8 chars)
insert logic: if bucket_count > 64 -> evict oldest session entry for that primary_key
result: mem growth flattened over 24h, hit-rate +9%, tail latency p99 down ~80ms (about 8% improvement).

infra-bot: deploy diff created: CL 4932; canary on one cluster? :white_check_mark:

pranav: CI perf tests? we need microbench for frequent short prompts to catch regressions.

ashley: added a benchmark simulating 10k users with short prefixes; results attached in the CL. Also added tracing points for primary_key churn.

sam: we should also consider prefix fingerprint collisions. maybe use 128-bit instead of 64. collision risk is tiny but cost of wrong reuse is high.

lisa: agree. pick 128-bit fingerprint and keep session short-id. Also add metric: unique_prefixes_per_min per host so ops can alert on abnormal fragmentation.

devon: long-term, we might want sticky routing so hot prefix owners stay on same host to reduce cross-host duplication. that pairs well with two-tier mapping.

ashley: good call. next steps I propose:
- land CL 4932 canary (safe config toggle)
- add unique_prefixes_per_min + primary_bucket_size histogram
- run 48h canary on two clusters with mixed traffic
- change fingerprint to 128-bit in separate CL after canary

pranav: sounds good. please ping infra when canary ready.

ashley: will do. thanks all :rocket:
